name: happy
description: The two-stage session-relevance walk: a cheap census of computer ids, then one tuple query over that id range. Proves the BESAPI XML is parsed at the shipped default property list, that the ~|~ multi-value separator is split back into individual values, that the OS short code is expanded and only a trailing dotted build number promoted to osVersion (the Red Hat string keeps its release in the name), that the RFC 1123 last report time is rebuilt into a parsable timestamp, and that the software property becomes Software with its version split out of both the 'name (1.2.3)' and 'name 1.2.3' forms. Computer 102 reports 127.0.0.1 as its only address and no MAC: it must still import, as an asset with no interface at all, because giving every agent that cannot read a NIC the same address would merge the estate onto one host. An unreadable census id, a blank tuple id, and a row of the wrong tuple width are each skipped with a count.
